owner.name: Delia Rhoades
owner.heading: The person on the ladder
owner.bio: Delia Rhoades started out washing storefronts along Seltice Way before sunrise, because that is the only hour a shop owner will let you block the door. She built Pane & Prairie around the two things those mornings taught her: a window is only clean if it is clean from the inside too, and the crew that made the mess is the crew that should carry it out. Delia still runs the pole on most jobs and answers the phone on all of them.

hero.subtitle: Pane & Prairie cleans windows inside and out across Post Falls and Kootenai County — glass, screens, tracks and sills, finished streak-free and dried by hand. Flat pricing by pane count, agreed before we unload a ladder.

about.heading: Most windows are half-cleaned, and everybody can tell
about.body: The outside gets a hose and the inside gets a paper towel, and the glass still hazes the second the sun hits it. We treat a window as four surfaces, not one: the exterior pane, the interior pane, the screen that has been filtering road dust all summer, and the track full of grit that dirties both again the next time you slide the sash. Do all four in one visit and the light comes through the way the builder intended.

howItWorks.title: Count and quote
howItWorks.desc: Tell us roughly how many panes you have, or send a couple of photos. We give you a flat number off the tier list before anyone shows up, and it does not move on the day.

howItWorks.title: Set up clean
howItWorks.desc: Drop cloths under every interior sill, ladder standoffs so nothing rests on your gutters or siding, and shoes off or booties on for the inside pass.

howItWorks.title: Wash, squeegee, detail
howItWorks.desc: Soap and scrub the pane, pull the squeegee in overlapping passes, then hand-dry the edges and corners with a dedicated cloth. Screens come out, get washed, and go back in the opening they came from.

howItWorks.title: Walk it with you
howItWorks.desc: We walk the house with you at low sun, which is when streaks show. Anything you point at gets redone right then. You pay when you are happy with the glass, not before.

included.title: Exterior glass
included.desc: Washed from ground level, water-fed pole or ladder, whichever the elevation calls for. No pressure washer anywhere near a seal.

included.title: Interior glass
included.desc: Cloths and drop sheets in every room, blinds lifted and returned to where you had them, no drips on the sill.

included.title: Screens
included.desc: Pulled, washed on both faces, dried and re-set in the same opening — screens are numbered as they come out so nothing ends up in the wrong window.

included.title: Tracks and sills
included.desc: Vacuumed first, then wiped out wet and dried. This is the step most quotes skip, and it is the one that keeps the glass clean longer.

included.title: Frames and mullions
included.desc: Hand-detailed so the white vinyl actually reads white, and the grid bars do not leave a dusty shadow across the pane.

included.title: Hard-water and paint spots
included.desc: Mineral etching from a sprinkler and construction overspray both come off with a separate process. We flag them at the quote so the price is honest before we begin.

niche.countHelp: Count a pane as one piece of glass you can see through. A double-hung window is two. A slider is two. A french-grid sash counts as one, not nine — the grid bars are frame, not glass.
niche.beforeAfterHeading: The same window, ten minutes apart
niche.beforeAfterBlurb: Drag the handle. Left is the pane soaped and still streaking; right is the same sash squeegeed, edged and dried — the tree and the brickwork outside are back.
niche.pricingNote: Every figure above is a flat rate for the whole visit, inside and out, screens and tracks included. Storey height, hard-water treatment and construction cleanup are quoted separately and always in writing first.

faq.q: Do I need to be home?
faq.a: For an exterior-only visit, no — leave the gate unlocked and we will text you when we are done. For an inside-and-out visit somebody needs to let us in, and we would rather you were there at the end for the walk-through anyway.

Second-story exteriors are routine, from a water-fed pole where the ground allows and a ladder with standoffs where it does not. Third storey and anything over a roofline gets looked at in person before we quote it.

faq.q: Will you get the hard-water spots off?
faq.a: Usually. Sprinkler overspray leaves mineral deposits that a normal wash will not touch, so they get a separate restoration pass. If the glass is etched past the point where that works, we will tell you rather than charge you to find out.

We work through most of the North Idaho year. Below freezing the water sheets and re-freezes on the glass, so winter jobs get rescheduled to the next workable day at no charge — you never lose a deposit, because we do not take one.

Twice a year suits most homes here — once after the spring pollen drops and once before the holidays. Storefronts on a dusty street usually want a monthly exterior route with a full inside pass a few times a year.
